subject: economics
topicDisplay: The Role Of Markets And Money
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: If price is set ABOVE the equilibrium price, the likely result is:
questions.explain: Above equilibrium, supply exceeds demand, creating a surplus that tends to push the price down.

questions.q: Which good is most likely to have price INELASTIC demand?
questions.explain: Necessities with few substitutes, such as fuel, tend to have inelastic demand.

questions.q: From a borrower's point of view, interest is:
questions.explain: For borrowers, interest is the price or cost paid for borrowing money.

questions.q: A negative externality of production is:
options: Always corrected by the free market
A cost imposed on third parties not involved in the transaction
A benefit to society greater than the private benefit
questions.explain: A negative externality is a spillover cost, such as pollution, borne by third parties.

questions.q: Interest, from a saver's point of view, is best described as:
options: The reward for saving or lending money
A fall in the value of money
questions.explain: Interest is the reward paid to savers and lenders for providing funds.

questions.q: A key feature of a monopoly compared with a competitive market is:
options: Free and easy entry for new firms
A single (or dominant) firm able to influence the price
questions.explain: A monopoly is a single dominant seller able to act as a price maker, unlike competitive price takers.

questions.q: Demand for a good is described as price INELASTIC when:
options: Quantity demanded changes a lot when price changes
The good has many close substitutes
Quantity demanded changes only a little when price changes
Demand falls to zero when price rises
questions.explain: Inelastic demand means quantity demanded is relatively unresponsive to a change in price.

questions.q: In a barter system (without money), a major problem is:
options: Needing a 'double coincidence of wants' to trade
questions.explain: Barter requires both parties to want what the other offers, a double coincidence of wants that money removes.

questions.q: If interest rates rise, people are generally encouraged to:
questions.explain: Higher interest rates increase the reward for saving and the cost of borrowing, so saving tends to rise.

questions.q: A demerit good, such as cigarettes, is one that:
options: Has no effect on third parties
Is over-consumed because consumers ignore its true costs
Is provided free by the government
questions.explain: Demerit goods are over-consumed because people underestimate their private and external costs.

questions.q: Money acts as a 'medium of exchange' because it:
options: Allows value to be saved for the future
Is widely accepted in return for goods and services
questions.explain: As a medium of exchange, money is generally accepted in payment, removing the need for barter.

questions.q: Borrowing money typically allows households to:
options: Bring spending forward, buying goods now and repaying later with interest
questions.explain: Borrowing lets households spend now and repay later, paying interest for the use of the funds.
